summary.one_liner: Ackee is a self-hosted, Node.js and MongoDB web analytics tool that tracks website traffic in an anonymized, cookie-free way.
summary.what_it_does: Ackee runs on your own server and analyzes traffic to your websites, presenting statistics in a minimal interface. It keeps tracked data anonymized so visitors are not identifiable, and it uses no cookies, so no cookie banner is needed. It can track custom events such as button clicks and newsletter subscriptions. Everything shown in the UI is driven by a fully documented GraphQL API, which can be used to build other tools. The README lists deployment routes including Docker Compose, Docker, Helm, plain Node.js, and several hosting platforms (Netlify, Vercel, Heroku, Qovery, Render, Railway, Koyeb, Zeabur), and configuration via environment variables or a .env file.
use_cases: tracking button clicks and newsletter signups
building custom stats dashboards via GraphQL
alternative to Google Analytics or Matomo
how_to_run: Configure via environment variables or a .env file in the project root
Configure SSL/HTTPS and CORS headers as described in the docs
notable: Cookie-free design with anonymized data, so no cookie consent message is required
Fully documented GraphQL API that the UI itself is built on
Event tracking for clicks and other custom actions
Many deployment options including Docker Compose, Helm and several PaaS hosts
Large ecosystem of related client plugins and trackers for frameworks like Gatsby, Nuxt, React and Django
caveats: Deliberately limited: the README says it is not meant for users needing a full-featured marketing analytics platform
Requires running your own server and a MongoDB database
Detailed setup guides are in the /docs folder rather than the README itself
